chapter: Orchestra people and Xavier chamber concerts
title: Paul Kosserbaum, symphony percussionist
summary: Kosserbaum is a quiet native New Orleans drummer who played percussion with Bill Hall in the symphony; Mazzari has no anecdotes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Oh, Paul Kosserbaum is an old time drummer, old New Orleanian from way back. He's a real nice boy. He... I didn't meet him until I came down to New Orleans and played in the symphony here. He was playing with Bill Hall. Bill Hall was in charge of the percussion section. And of course, invariably, there are two men back there, you know, to play the bass drum, the snare drums, the triangles, the bells, you know, how the percussion section is in the symphony orchestra. And I got to meet Paul Kosserbaum and he's a very quiet, easy going fellow. And he'd been living... He was born here in New Orleans and lived here all his life. And a very nice cat.
You don't remember any little anecdotes about him or Fontana or anybody else?
Oh, no, not off the handle, I couldn't tell you. I mean...
